result:
FINDING: app/auth.py:14 | security | high | `find_user` builds SQL with an f-string around the attacker-controlled `name`, which allows SQL injection, including login bypass through `check_login`.
FINDING: app/auth.py:5 | security | high | `SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded in source, so anyone with the code can forge tokens from `sign_token`.
FINDING: app/files.py:10 | security | high | `export_report` joins the caller-supplied `filename` into the path with no `basename` or containment check, so `../` or an absolute path writes outside `EXPORT_DIR`.
FINDING: app/auth.py:9 | security | medium | The password salt is the username, so it is predictable rather than a random per-user salt.
FINDING: app/auth.py:35 | security | medium | The token is an HMAC over only `user_id`, with no expiry, nonce or audience, so it can be replayed forever.
FINDING: app/orders.py:13 | logic | high | `apply_discount` uses `>` but the docstring says orders of $100.00 or more get the discount, so exactly 10,000 cents gets none.
FINDING: app/orders.py:23 | logic | high | Tax is computed on `subtotal` instead of the discounted amount, which contradicts the docstring.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:10 | logic | high | The slice ends at `start + page_size - 1`, so every page returns one item too few.
FINDING: app/orders.py:61 | logic | medium | `place_order` ignores the return value of `reserve` and commits per line, so a mid-cart failure leaves partial reservations and the order is still created. Repeated SKUs can also oversell.
FINDING: app/orders.py:35 | performance | medium | `dedupe_skus` checks `sku not in seen` on a list, which is O(n²); a companion set would make it O(n).
FINDING: app/orders.py:44 | performance | low | `count_by_status` rescans all orders once per status instead of making a single pass.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:21 | tests | high | `test_discount_at_threshold` only prints the result and has no assertion, so it hides the `>` vs `>=` bug. The bug-hunter put this at line 19; I used the test-reviewer's line 21 and did not check the file.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:7 | tests | high | `assert len(page) <= 10` passes even though `paginate` returns one item short; it should assert the exact page length.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:25 | tests | medium | The only `order_total` test uses a subtotal below the discount threshold, so the tax-on-undiscounted-subtotal bug goes uncaught.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:25 | tests | low | The export/read round trip never checks the path `export_report` returns or that `read_report` strips directory components, so a path-traversal regression would pass.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:14 | tests | low | `test_find_user` covers only the happy path, with no test for a missing user or a quote character in the name.

The bug-hunter reported `orders.py` and `inventory.py` without a directory, and I assumed they are in `app/`. I merged the duplicate reports of the `auth.py` and `files.py` issues into the security entries above. I didn't open any files myself, so these line numbers are the reviewers' own.
